name: fig2-ga-intervention
title: Fig 2 / Table 1 — GA-identified intervention lowers mortality
question: Can a genetic algorithm over multi-stage cytokine augmentation/inhibition — the paper's control-discovery method — find an intervention that lowers IIRABM mortality, and does mortality fall as more sequential interventions are applied (Table 1)?
experiment: Run a reduced-scale GA (tournament selection size 2, uniform crossover, per-gene values from {0.05,0.25,0.5,0.75,1,2,5,10,20}) against the real IIRABM, minimizing oxygen deficit + infection across replicate seeds. Report the convergence curve, the discovered intervention (Fig 2-style log2 bars), the mortality reduction vs untreated, and the mortality-vs-#interventions curve (Table 1). The paper's production GA used ~1e6 CPU-hours; this reproduces the method at laptop scale.

behavior_tests.name: ga-lowers-mortality
behavior_tests.description: The GA-discovered intervention lowers population mortality below the untreated baseline. Pass if GA-intervention mortality < baseline mortality.

visualizations.name: ga-convergence
visualizations.description: GA best-fitness per generation (oxygen deficit + infection; lower = healthier).

visualizations.name: ga-intervention-bars
visualizations.description: The GA-discovered intervention as log2 multiplier bars per cytokine per stage (Fig 2 style).

visualizations.name: mortality-vs-interventions
visualizations.description: Mortality vs number of sequential interventions applied (Table 1).

report.verdict: GA method reproduced against the genuine model (fitness converges 2340->1048) and its intervention is marginally beneficial (77.5% vs 80% untreated). The dramatic mortality reduction in the paper requires supercomputer-scale search and is not reproduced at laptop scale — consistent with the paper's thesis that effective control demands a very large, multi-targeted search.

result: GA fitness 2340->1048; GA-intervention mortality 77.5% < baseline 80% (primary test PASSES, marginal).
